newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PENGUINS, CANADIENS TIE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PENGUINS, CANADIENS TIE.

text.p: PITTSBURGH, Jaromir Jagr's shorthanded goal with 9:18 left in the third period lifted the Pittsburgh Penguins into a 2-2 tie with the Montreal Canadiens on Wednesday.

With Mario Lemieux off for slashing, Jagr stole the puck from Scott Thornton and Marc Bureau and broke into the Canadiens' zone alone. He skated down the slot and slid left. Jocelyn Thibault committed and Jagr shot high into the open right side for his league-leading 19th goal.
"On a breakaway, you have to try and react to what they give you," observed Jagr. "Thibault made the first move and I held on to it a little longer."
In Anaheim, Robert Petrovicky scored the game-winner midway through the third period in his Blues' debut, lifting St. Louis past the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim, 3-2.
Petrovicky, recalled from the minors earlier in the week, took a pass from Chris Pronger low in the left faceoff circle, spun and wristed a shot under the crossbar with just over 11 minutes to play.
In Colorado, Mark Messier and Pat Flatley each scored twice and Mike Richter made 31 saves as the New York Rangers surprised the Colorado Avalanche, 5-2 for a split of their six-game road trip.
"We're still four or five games under .500, so we're not going home thinking that we have turned the season. We still have a lot of work to do," said Messier.
Colorado was leading 1-0 when Alexei Kovalev passed from behind the net to Messier, who wristed the puck past Patrick Roy at 10:01 of the first period.
New York took the lead for good just 38 seconds on Flatley's goal.
In Dallas, John MacLean's breakaway goal with 1:56 remaining gave the New Jersey Devils a 3-2 victory over the Dallas Stars.
"We caught them on a line change and Scottie hit me with a great pass," MacLean said. "We stayed in there for 60 minutes."
Rookie Mike Dunham made 31 saves for New Jersey, which carried a 2-0 lead into the third period.
Jamie Langenbrunner and Dave Reid scored for Dallas.

In Detroit, Brendan Shanahan recorded his eighth career hat trick and Darren McCarty had a goal and an assist as the Detroit Red Wings handed the Toronto Maple Leafs their seventh straight road loss, 5-2.

Shanahan completed his first hat trick as a Red Wing at 10:20 of the second period, beating goaltender Felix Potvin with a one-timer from the right faceoff circle and putting Detroit ahead for good, 3-2.
In Edmonton, Byron Dafoe came within five seconds of a shutout and five different players scored as the Los Angeles Kings broke a three-game losing streak with a 5-1 victory over the Edmonton Oilers.
Luke Richardson scored his first goal of the season at 19:55 of the third period to spoil Dafoe's shutout bid. Dafoe made 37 saves, including 18 in the second period, to improve to 6-2.

In Hartford, Alexander Mogilny had two goals and three assists and linemate Mike Ridley added two goals and two assists, leading the Vancouver Canucks to their fourth win in five games, 6-2 over the Hartford Whalers.
Corey Hirsch made 41 saves for the Canucks, who improved to 1-1 on their six-game road trip.
At the Islanders, Tommy Salo made 29 saves and Marty McInnis scored twice as the New York Islanders beat the Philadelphia Flyers for the third time this season, 4-1.
Salo stopped 12 shots in the third period, including shorthanded breakaways during the same penalty by Shjon Podein and Rod Brind'Amour.
New York moved ahead of Tampa Bay into sixth place in the Atlantic Division.

In San Jose, Tony Granato's power-play tally, his 200th career goal, capped a three-goal second period as the San Jose Sharks snapped a six-game winless streak with a 3-2 defeat of the Chicago Blackhawks.
After a scoreless first period, Jeff Friesen, Darren Turcotte and Granato scored in a 10-minute span of the second as the Sharks won for the first time since November 8th.

At Tampa Bay, Dominik Hasek recorded his second shutout of the season and Brian Holzinger, Curtis Brown and Randy Burridge scored in the third period to give the Buffalo Sabres a 3-0 victory over the floundering Tampa Bay Lightning.
Hasek made 28 of his 32 saves over the final two periods, but Buffalo limited the Lightning primarily to perimeter shots.
In Washington, Lance Pitlick's goal with 52 seconds left in the second period snapped a tie and lifted the Ottawa Senators to a 2-1 victory over the Washington Capitals.
Former Capital Ron Tugnutt made 31 saves to earn his second win.
